summary:
EarthWatch AI is an interactive Earth observation and climate trend detection platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms complex Earth science datasets into meaningful visual insights, helping users investigate how our planet is changing over time.

The platform integrates NASA Earth observation resources, including NASA POWER, GLDAS, MODIS and other supported environmental data services, alongside NOAA climate observations. Users can explore geographical regions, analyze environmental variables such as temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation health and land surface temperature, and visualize historical trends through interactive charts and maps.

Using statistical methods such as linear regression, Mann-Kendall testing and Sen's slope estimation, EarthWatch AI helps identify and interpret significant environmental trends. Google Gemini further supports accessibility by converting calculated results into easy-to-understand scientific explanations.

This project addresses the challenge by making Earth system trend detection more accessible, interactive and understandable. Its ultimate goal is to empower students, researchers and communities to explore environmental changes and make more informed, evidence-based decisions for a sustainable future.
details:
EarthWatch AI – Earth System Trend Detective

Project Overview

EarthWatch AI is an interactive Earth observation and climate trend analysis platform designed to help people understand how our planet is changing over time. It transforms complex environmental datasets into accessible visual insights, allowing users to investigate climate patterns, compare geographical regions, and identify statistically detectable environmental trends.

How It Works

Users can select a geographical location, choose an environmental variable, and define a time period for investigation. The application retrieves available time-series data from NASA and other supported environmental data services. Users can explore the results through interactive charts, maps, and analysis dashboards.

The platform supports investigations of variables such as:

  • Near-surface air temperature.
  • Precipitation and rainfall.
  • Soil moisture.
  • Vegetation health (NDVI).
  • Land surface temperature.

It applies statistical techniques such as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, Mann–Kendall trend testing, Sen's slope estimation, seasonal analysis, and confidence intervals where supported by the selected analysis workflow.

Users can also compare multiple locations, examine anomalies, review missing-data information, and explore explanations of the observed trends.

Benefits and Intended Impact

EarthWatch AI makes Earth science data easier to explore and understand. It can help students, educators, researchers, environmental enthusiasts, and decision-makers investigate climate variability and long-term environmental changes.

Its intended impact includes:

  • Improving public understanding of climate change and environmental trends.
  • Making scientific data analysis more accessible.
  • Helping users identify regional environmental patterns.
  • Encouraging evidence-based environmental awareness.
  • Supporting educational research and climate literacy.

Technology and Tools Used

The project is developed using:

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.
  • Data visualization: Plotly.js, Recharts and Leaflet.
  • Geospatial and 3D visualization: Three.js and React Three Fiber.
  • Data management: TanStack Query and Zustand.
  • Environmental data services: NASA POWER, NASA Earthdata, NASA CMR, NASA AppEEARS, NASA GES DISC/Giovanni, GLDAS and NOAA Climate Data Online.
  • Testing: Vitest and Playwright.

Creativity and Innovation

The innovative aspect of EarthWatch AI is its combination of environmental data discovery, geographical exploration, statistical trend detection, and accessible scientific explanations in one platform.

Instead of simply displaying climate charts, the application helps users investigate whether observed changes represent statistically detectable trends. It also emphasizes data quality, uncertainty, missing observations, and the limitations of scientific interpretation.

The platform is designed around the idea of turning users into Earth System Trend Detectives, allowing them to investigate their own questions about our changing planet.

Factors Considered During Development

We considered scientific reliability, data availability, geographical coverage, temporal resolution, missing observations, statistical significance, usability, accessibility, and the differences between satellite-derived, model-based, and station-based measurements.

We also considered that statistical correlation or a detected trend does not automatically establish its physical cause. Therefore, the application aims to present environmental evidence transparently rather than making unsupported scientific conclusions.Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

Our project, EarthWatch AI, uses Super Intelligence tools responsibly to improve accessibility, communication, and the development process.

1. AI Tools Used

  • Google Gemini API: Integrated into the application to generate natural-language explanations of environmental trend analysis and optional AI-generated voice narration.
  • AI-assisted development tools: Any additional tools used by the development team for coding assistance, debugging, documentation, or brainstorming are acknowledged according to their actual use.

2. How SI Was Used

Gemini helps translate computed statistical results into understandable scientific explanations for students and general users. It is instructed to use only the numerical results supplied by the application and avoid unsupported causal claims.

Optional voice narration uses AI-generated speech to make scientific findings more accessible.

3. Code and Data Transparency

The statistical calculations and environmental trend results are computed by the application's analysis code using retrieved environmental datasets. AI-generated explanations do not replace the underlying statistical calculations.

Environmental observations and datasets are obtained from their respective data providers. AI-generated interpretations are distinguished from source data and calculated scientific results.

4. Images, Videos and Audio

Any AI-generated images or videos used in the final project will be visibly labelled as AI-generated. Any AI-generated voice narration will be acknowledged in its accompanying description and metadata.

5. Human Oversight

Our team remains responsible for reviewing the scientific explanations, checking data sources, validating the analysis, and ensuring that the application communicates uncertainty and limitations honestly.

We have not used AI to impersonate NASA, reproduce NASA branding, or imply official NASA endorsement.
